paper_title: SepLLM Accelerate Large Language Models by Compressing One Segment into   One Separator
caption: : Loss steps

annotations.annotation: The line plot illustrates the change in loss values over iterations for different models. The x-axis is labeled "#Iteration" and uses a linear scale, ranging from 0 to 140,000 with tick labels at intervals of 20,000. The y-axis is labeled "Loss" and also uses a linear scale, ranging from 2.4 to 3.4, with tick labels at intervals of 0.1. The plot contains several lines: a purple line representing "Vanilla" which starts around a loss of more than 3.4 at 0 iterations and decreases more sharply at first till 2.7, steadily decreases to approximately 2.45 by 140,000 iterations; a blue line for "StrmLLM (n=64)" starts near 3.4 and decreases more sharply at first till 2.9, a final value around 2.6; an orange line for "SepLLM (n=64)" begins close to 3.4 and decreases more sharply at first till 2.8, steadily decreases to about 2.52; a green line for "SepLLM (n=64, H)" which also starts near 3.4 and decreases more sharply at first till 2.8, ends closer to 2.5; a red line labeled "SepLLM (n=64, H/T)" that starts at 3.4 and decreases more sharply at first till 2.7, declines steadily to around 2.48; and a dark blue line for "SepLLM (n=128)" which begins at about 3.4 and decreases more sharply at first till 2.8, ends around 2.5. All lines show a general downward trend indicating decreasing loss over iterations. All lines have minor fluctuations throughout, and then each has variance in light color. A legend is given in top right.
